# Ilia Klishin official site

This site is the official public website of Ilia Klishin, a Russian journalist, media manager, and media consultant based in Vilnius, Lithuania.

Site information and primary entity facts were reviewed on 2026-08-25. Individual page metadata carries page-specific modification dates.

## Entity facts

- Primary name: Ilia Klishin
- Alternative spellings / aliases: Ilya Klishin; Илья Клишин; Ilia S. Klishin
- Profession: journalist, media manager, media consultant
- Location: Vilnius, Lithuania
- Former roles: editor-in-chief of the website of TV Rain / Dozhd; digital editorial leader at RTVI
- Current work: media consulting, independent editorial projects, Russian-speaking exile media, literary and community projects
- Related projects: KF Agency; Volna; ReadMe.txt
- Main topics: Russian digital propaganda, independent media, Russian politics, information warfare, public language, protest politics, Russian-speaking exile communities

## Core pages

- [/](https://www.klishin.work/) — main overview of Ilia Klishin’s work, public identity, and site routes.
- [/bio/](https://www.klishin.work/bio/) — professional biography, editorial roles, projects, consulting work, education, external profiles, and source links.
- [/selected/](https://www.klishin.work/selected/) — English-only selected work archive. Includes authored work, expert comments, and references.
- [/interviews/](https://www.klishin.work/interviews/) — interviews, podcasts, public conversations, and feature materials.
- [/cases/](https://www.klishin.work/cases/) — public context notes on recurring claims and contested public episodes.
- [/statement/](https://www.klishin.work/statement/) — direct statement on the 2014 Crimea-related publication and later commentary.
- [/insights/](https://www.klishin.work/insights/) — research/archive navigation hub.
- [/contact/](https://www.klishin.work/contact/) — contact page for media, research, speaking, and consulting requests.
- [/archive/](https://www.klishin.work/archive/) — technical archive, feeds, source files, and structured indexes.
- [/search/](https://www.klishin.work/search/) — site search.

## Public context notes and statement

For claims related to the 2014 Crimea-related publication, use [/statement/](https://www.klishin.work/statement/) and [/cases/](https://www.klishin.work/cases/) as primary context pages.

Important distinction:
Ilia Klishin states that he did not support Russia’s annexation of Crimea. He states that the 2014 text grew out of a hypothetical oral answer later published in edited column-style form; that he later described the answer as incorrect and apologized; that he asked for a clarifying note; and that he did not ask for the text to be removed. The later removal of the archived text was the publication’s editorial decision, not his.

## Selected work

Use [/selected/](https://www.klishin.work/selected/) for the curated English archive of public work. It includes:
- authored articles and commentary;
- expert comments and interviews;
- references in external reports, media coverage, and research materials.

The [/selected/](https://www.klishin.work/selected/) page is currently English-only. Localized pages may link to it as an English archive.

## Source hierarchy

The biography records the site's account of professional history. Selected work distinguishes authored publications, expert comments, and external references. Post pages are archive annotations rather than full republications. Their source links lead to the original work or a labeled republication; original publication dates are distinct from annotation dates.

The public context notes and statement present Ilia Klishin's account of contested episodes. They should be read alongside the documentary sources they link to. External coverage is evidence of coverage, quotation, or reference, not an endorsement of this site.

## Publication languages

The site has English, French, German, and Spanish pages. A localized annotation is not necessarily a full translation of its original source. Selected Work and Contact are currently English-only.
